newsitem.title: UK: Tin physicals slow in Europe, premiums hold stable.
newsitem.headline: Tin physicals slow in Europe, premiums hold stable.

text.p: Physical tin business is currently running at a low ebb in Europe, with end-users mostly content to hold off, as they are adequately stocked at present, traders said.
Partly, this is because there is still an overhang from the consumer inventory builds of 1996, but it is also due to currency factors and hesitation over current price levels, they said.
"Business is rotten at the moment - it is nearly non-existent," one European trader said.
Tin prices slipped back on the London Metal Exchange (LME) on Tuesday to around $5,920 a tonne, without generating much end-user interest.
There was some talk of Chinese selling in the market, possibly ahead of China's New Year holidays early next month.
"There has been a bit of a price dip, but we are not seeing much interest. I guess that consumers are still looking for lower numbers," another trader said.
Also, there has been a growing trend in the market for producers and consumers to deal direct and lock in frame deals, leaving the traders more on the sidelines.
And the strength of the dollar against most European currencies means that the slight price dip has had little real impact on Continental end-users.
"We have heard that there is some enquiry for five or 10 tonne parcels, but they have not booked any quantities," the European trader added.
Meanwhile, the larger end-users in the market, such as steel companies who would typically purchase 100 to 200 tonne clips, are similarly holding off at present.

Because there is an inventory overhang, the market may remain quiet for the rest of this quarter, and possibly beyond, unless there is a dramatic decline in the price which would encourage re-stocking, traders added.

Premiums are hardly moving from recent levels, which are themselves below end-1996 ideas. There is very little Brazilian MAMORE available, so indications were scant, while varying lead contents made for nominal Russian quotes.
